evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with progressive neurological disease (exemplified by motor neurone disease): respiratory monitoring and NIV, nutrition and gastrostomy, cramps, spasticity, saliva and end-of-life planning. Verified against NICE NG42 (MND); doses from FDA labels and MOH Protocol-010.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Quinine and glycopyrronium doses — local protocol
Other progressive neurological diseases (Parkinson's, MS) not individually covered

pathophysiology.summary: Progressive neurological diseases cause worsening weakness, swallowing and respiratory failure. In MND, respiratory muscle weakness is the main cause of death, so regular respiratory assessment and timely NIV and gastrostomy discussions are central.
keyMechanisms: Motor neurone loss weakens limb, bulbar and respiratory muscles.
Bulbar weakness → dysphagia, drooling, aspiration, weight loss.
Respiratory weakness → nocturnal hypoventilation (orthopnoea, morning headache) then hypercapnic failure.

symptoms: Weakness, cramps, stiffness, drooling, choking, breathlessness, orthopnoea, poor sleep, morning headache, weight loss.
physicalSigns: Wasting, fasciculations, spasticity, weak cough; reduced FVC.
redFlags: PaCO2 above 6 kPa — urgent respiratory ventilation service referral within 1 week (NICE NG42)
precipitants: Motor neurone disease; other progressive neurological disease

ruleIn.expectedFinding: FVC/VC below 50% predicted; SNIP/MIP below 40 cmH2O; or FVC below 80% / SNIP below 65 (men) or 55 (women) cmH2O with symptoms; SNIP fall above 10 cmH2O per 3 months.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Discuss impairment and consider referral to respiratory ventilation service (NICE NG42 Table 2).
ruleIn.normalValue: FVC 80% predicted or more; SNIP above 65 (men) / 55 (women) cmH2O

clinicalManagement.title: Respiratory
actions: Offer NIV for respiratory impairment, decided by MDT with the ventilation service; explain it can be stopped at any time (NICE NG42).

clinicalManagement.title: Nutrition
actions: Discuss gastrostomy early and at intervals, considering swallow, weight, respiratory function and choking risk (NICE NG42).

clinicalManagement.title: Symptoms
actions: Cramps: quinine first line; baclofen second line (NICE NG42) — baclofen 5 mg three times daily, increasing every 3 days (label).
Stiffness/spasticity: baclofen, tizanidine, dantrolene or gabapentin (NICE NG42).
Drooling: advice on posture and oral care; glycopyrronium first line if cognitive impairment (NICE NG42) — dose per local protocol.

clinicalManagement.title: End of life
actions: Discuss preferences at diagnosis, respiratory change or before gastrostomy/NIV; review advance decisions (NICE NG42 1.7).
Prompt access to anticipatory opioids and benzodiazepines for breathlessness and antimuscarinics for secretions (NICE NG42).

learningObjectives: Support people with progressive neurological disease through respiratory, nutritional, symptom and end-of-life care.
